order.text: In Recent years, Text-to-Image (T2I) Generative Models have witnessed impressive advances, yielding unprecedented photorealistic quality. These advances have been driven by Models optimized for human preference. performance improvements for These Models are usually reported in terms of image realism and prompt-image consistency, with well-established metrics (Heusel et al., 2018; Kynkäänniemi et al., 2019; Naeem et al., 2020; Hessel et al., 2021; Hu et al., 2023b; Cho et al., 2024; Lin et al., 2024). However, optimizing for human preference alone has led to state-of-the-art Models having limited representation Diversity (Hall et al., 2024; Sehwag et al., 2022; Zameshina et al., 2023; Corso et al., 2023; Askari Hemmat et al., 2023; Hemmat et al., 2024; Sadat et al., 2023).

For example, Most Models fail to differentiate between “open” and “closed” attributes when explicitly asked to do so through dense prompts. Sometimes they fail to consistently generate the “closed” attribute, While other times they fail to consistently generate “open” concepts. However, Models are able to generate both “open” and “closed” attributes when generating images through coarse prompts. which means that the Models fail to generate certain attributes when explicitly asked, but generates them in Default-mode. such examples of “closed-wings” birds generated by LDM3.5L (Esser et al., 2024) and “full” refrigerators generated by Flow-Int are shown in Figure 5. We include more examples in the Supplementary Materials.

order.text: T2I Models struggle with negations. For example, Figure 4 shows that all Models have low Can-it Metric scores for the concept bed when negation attributes “Without blanket” and “Without pillows,” generating images of blankets and pillows even when explicitly asked not to generate those. this is also observed by previous work (Conwell et al., 2024), and demonstrates the efficacy of DIMCIM in serving as an automatic identifier of established failure modes.

additions.summary: Consistency metrics (including CLIPScore-style and VQA-based approaches like TIFA and VQAScore)
DIMCIM uses a modified VQAScore that considers only the specific attribute-object pair, avoiding the need for an external LLM for question generation and mitigating linguistic biases
